title: the Undercroft Rising
premise: Ulyana Halloran, a late-night radio host in the decaying city of Ashgrave, has spent three years fielding calls from listeners who died days earlier — voices she has convinced herself are grief-driven hoaxes or signal bleed. When her own sleep recordings reveal a second voice answering her questions in her cadence, she learns the callers are echoes of the forty-one people entombed beneath the old Undercroft in 1974, and that her mother was the one who sealed them in to survive. To free the dead — and the fragment of herself they have been growing in the dark — Ulyana must return what was taken: her own name, given away at birth as the price of her mother's escape. In the end she speaks her true name on air, dissolves the Undercroft's hold, and survives as someone new, half-remembered even by herself.
about_author: E. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former hospital archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed belongings and now writes horror about the things people leave behind in themselves. They live in a coastal town with poor cell reception and a well-documented history of missing persons.

chapters.title: Dead Air, Warm Voices
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. During a broadcast, a caller describes her studio in perfect detail — a man whose obituary ran six days ago. She rationalizes it as a prank, but her hands shake through the rest of the shift. The emotional beat is the first crack in three years of careful denial: the horror of realizing the explanations are running out.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with transcript excerpts. Reviewing her sleep-recording app for an unrelated reason, she finds nights of dialogue: a voice identical to hers asking questions, and a wet, patient voice answering. It knows things only she knows — and things she doesn't. Beat: violated intimacy; the self as haunted house.

chapters.title: Forty-One Below
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, interleaved with 1974 newspaper fragments. Researching the Undercroft, a municipal bathhouse basement where forty-one people vanished during a flood, she finds her mother's maiden name on the survivor list — the only name on it. Beat: dread curdling into inheritance; the past is not past, it's downstairs.

chapters.title: What Mother Gave Away
chapters.summary: Ulyana travels to her dying mother's care facility. Sedated, her mother confesses: to leave the Undercroft alive, she traded her infant's true name to the thing below, and it has been growing a child of its own ever since. Beat: betrayal and pity braided together — survival has a receipt, and it's addressed to Ulyana.

chapters.title: The Caller Who Was Me
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On air, a caller speaks in her exact voice, reciting her sleep-talk verbatim, then says: 'Come down, or I come up.' Listeners phone in reporting the studio's signal bleeding into their dreams. Beat: the private horror goes public; Ulyana realizes she is the broadcast now.

chapters.title: Descent, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She enters the flooded Undercroft with a recorder and a crowbar, finds forty-one alcoves like radio booths, each humming with a voice. Her recorder plays her mother's 1974 confession back at her before she speaks it. Beat: claustrophobic awe — the dead aren't imprisoned here; they're being kept, like archives.

chapters.title: The Name in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, dissolving into the double's. The second voice — her un-named twin, grown for fifty years — offers a trade: its name for hers, freedom for both. Ulyana nearly accepts, feeling more at home below than above. Beat: temptation; identity as the thing you'd surrender to survive.

chapters.title: Signal Lost
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, frayed and unreliable. Trapped by rising water, she loses hours and wakes in her own bed, unsure she ever left — until she finds silt under her nails and her on-air voice now speaking in the twin's cadence. Beat: identity unraveling; she can no longer tell which voice is the recording.

chapters.title: The Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. She hijacks the station's transmitter and broadcasts from the Undercroft itself, giving the dead forty-one names back on air so the city remembers them. The twin demands its price; Ulyana speaks her true name — the one her mother sold — and the name tears free, taking the twin's hold with it. Beat: sacrifice as reclamation; memory as the only exorcism.

chapters.title: Someone New, Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, quiet aftermath. The Undercroft is a dry concrete shell; the callers are gone; her mother dies at peace. Ulyana keeps broadcasting under a name that no longer quite fits, comfortable in the gap where the old one was. Final beat: survival didn't return her to who she was — it made room for who she's choosing to be.
